record.paper_title: Ten Open Problems in Grammatical Inference
record.original_question: What is the learnability theory for ordinary, non-deterministic partially observable Markov decision processes with probabilistic transitions and reward functions? The problem is to study learnability for the general POMDP model, not only the deterministic special case, and to clarify suitable success criteria such as identification in the limit with probability 1, regret-based convergence, or relations to strategy learning.

evidence.quote: Partialy Observable Markov Decision Processes are an extension of Markov Decision Processes, these being related to Hidden Markov Models.
Problem 8. Study the learnability of ordinary Pomdp s.
Identification in the limit with probability 1 is an issue. But using convergence criteria from reinforcement learning (such as regret) is probably a better idea.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) is a tuple $M=(S,A,O,T,Z,R,\iota)$ where $S$ is a finite set of states, $A$ a finite set of actions, $O$ a finite set of observations, $T:S\times A\times S\to[0,1]$ a transition probability function with $\sum_{s'}T(s,a,s')=1$, $Z:S\times A\times O\to[0,1]$ an observation probability function with $\sum_{o}Z(s,a,o)=1$, $R:S\times A\to\mathbb{R}$ a reward function, and $\iota$ an initial distribution over $S$. A learner interacts with $M$ by choosing actions and receiving observations and rewards, without access to the underlying states. 

Develop a learnability theory for the class of all (general, probabilistic, non-deterministic) POMDPs in this sense. Concretely:

1. Identify a precise success criterion for learning a POMDP from interaction data — for instance (a) identification in the limit with probability 1 of the underlying model (up to equivalence preserving the distribution over observation/reward sequences under every policy), (b) convergence of the learner's average regret with respect to the optimal policy of $M$ to zero, or (c) convergence in the sense of strategy learning, where the learner's policy converges to an optimal policy of $M$.

2. For the chosen criterion, determine whether the class of all POMDPs (or natural subclasses such as those satisfying explicit identifiability/observability conditions) is learnable, and if so provide a learning algorithm together with sample- or interaction-complexity bounds.

3. Clarify the relationships between the criteria in (1) and between learnability of POMDPs and learnability of related models such as hidden Markov models, probabilistic finite automata, and Markov decision processes.

The deterministic special case (deterministic transitions and observations) should be recovered as a particular instance of the theory.
artifact.status_search_result: The general learnability theory for POMDPs in the grammatical-inference identification-in-the-limit sense remains open. While substantial progress exists in the reinforcement-learning literature on regret/sample-complexity bounds for POMDPs under structural assumptions (e.g., hindsight observability, weakly revealing or decodable POMDPs), no unified learnability theory analogous to that for DFAs/PFAs exists for the general probabilistic POMDP model, and the problem continues to be cited as open.

status_evidence.title: Ten Open Problems in Grammatical Inference
status_evidence.snippet: Lists learning POMDPs among open problems in grammatical inference.
status_evidence.claim: The learnability of ordinary POMDPs is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Learning in POMDPs is Sample-Efficient with Hindsight Observability
status_evidence.snippet: Provides sample-efficient learning results under hindsight observability assumptions, not the general POMDP case.
status_evidence.claim: Recent positive learnability results require structural assumptions, indicating the general case remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: An Extension of Finite-state MDP and an Application of Grammatical Inference
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses challenges of POMDP learning due to partial state identification from observations.
status_evidence.claim: General POMDP learnability remains challenging; only restricted cases are addressed.
